title: Preoperative risk assessment of the difficult airway: a gender-specific comparison of established scores.
summary: The aim of the study is to investigate the reliability of common clinical tests for assessing a difficult airway prior to surgery. Particular attention will be paid to whether these tests work differently for women and men. For this purpose, various characteristics such as mouth opening or jaw mobility are measured before anesthesia and compared with the actual course of intubation. The results should help to increase patient safety and tailor the planning of anaesthesia even more specifically to individual needs.

interventions.name:
Arm 1 comprises adult patients undergoing anesthesiological management with endotracheal intubation as part of a surgical procedure.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Only binary individuals (female/male) aged 18 years and older who are scheduled for a planned surgical procedure under intubation anesthesia are included. The focus on binary genders serves to specifically investigate gender-specific differences in the predictive validity of established airway scores. In addition, the small number of non-binary people may jeopardize anonymity.
Exclusion criteria:
Persons under the age of 18 and patients who are pregnant are excluded from participation. Patients with known anatomical abnormalities in the oronasopharyngeal region or with previous surgical interventions in this region are also not included in the study, as these factors could significantly influence the standardized assessment of the airway situation and thus limit the comparability of the data.
